answer: Agents can earn influence only after completing a random, beacon-timed challenge: a falcon verifier selects a task, then checks the response against evidence from independent sparrow witnesses with distinct, stake-backed histories. Repeated identities controlled by one attacker tend to share infrastructure or fail to produce independent evidence, so clustering and slashing can expose them. Passing still costs the attacker real resources: each identity needs a separate stake, sustained useful work, and the risk of losing collateral when caught.
